findings.summary: Lessons file documents committing/pushing with `--no-verify` to bypass the verify pipeline, presented as an accepted workaround rather than flagged as an exception.
findings.evidence: "The commit/push used `--no-verify`; the touched lanes (backend analytics jest, frontend vitest, frontend eslint) were run individually and CI covers the rest." — while the note explains the pre-existing unrelated typecheck failure that motivated it and lists mitigations, it still normalizes bypassing the local verification hook as a way to get a commit/push through, which is the kind of practice future readers could copy without the same care.

findings.summary: New 403-specific error message in DocumentAnalyticsPage has no test
findings.evidence: The diff adds a distinct rendering branch: `error instanceof HttpError && error.status === 403` renders a permission-specific message instead of "Failed to load analytics." No test exercises either branch. There is no test file for document-analytics.tsx (globbed packages/frontend/src/app/analytics/** — only date-range.test.ts, format.test.ts, series.test.ts, views-trend-chart.test.tsx exist), and the new test added by this PR (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-analytics.test.tsx) covers only the ranking page. So nothing verifies that getDocumentAnalytics actually surfaces an `HttpError` instance with `.status === 403` through react-query (it goes through `assertOk` in api/http-error.ts and `fetchWithAuth`); if the thrown error were wrapped or a different class, the page would silently keep showing the generic text and every suite would still be green.

findings.summary: Hand-rolled SQL quoting for StarRocks escapes only single quotes, not backslashes
findings.evidence: `sql()` (analytics-warehouse.service.ts:33-35) builds every warehouse predicate by string interpolation (`buildQueries` line 89, `buildWorkspaceQueries` line 152; the `byDocument` query feeding the `documentRows` mapper touched by this diff at line 226) and escapes only `'` by doubling. StarRocks speaks the MySQL protocol, where a trailing backslash in a literal escapes the closing quote (`'a\'` swallows the delimiter), so a value ending in `\` would let the remainder of the string continue the SQL expression — e.g. `... document_id = 'x\' AND 1=1 OR '` — reading arbitrary `view_events` rows across workspaces. I could not complete the vector: the only strings reaching `sql()` are `day()` output (derived from `Date`, safe) and document ids, and ids are server-generated UUIDs (`prisma/schema.prisma:42 id String @default(uuid())`) that must round-trip a `findUnique`/`findMany` before being interpolated, so no attacker-controlled string currently reaches the quoter. Reported as a defense-in-depth gap on the escaping helper; it is pre-existing code, not added by this diff.
